llm.summary: The bond market gave equities a breather: Treasury yields reversed from 2002 highs, Brent slipped below $100, and the Nasdaq printed a record with Nvidia at an all-time high on Foxconn's Q3 revenue surge and a $108bn Q3 outlook. But the relief is narrow — Technology flows are at +84 while every other sector sits between -11 and -89, and growth is now beating value by 99 points (94 yesterday), the widest in this series. Gold recovered off two-month lows above $4,100 precisely because oil fell and nominal yields cooled, confirming that real yields and the dollar, not Fed pricing, remain the binding constraint on hard assets. The regime shifted in a telling way overnight: Contraction fell 6.8 and Goldilocks fell 4.3, while Reflation (+6.1) and Stagflation (+5.0) both rose — the market is re-pricing toward higher nominal growth with sticky prices, not toward a clean soft landing. Power is where the AI trade got physical: Google signed a 20-year, $1bn-plus nuclear PPA with Constellation and Meta funded seven gas plants for its largest data center, while Utilities flows sit at -84 — the single cleanest dislocation on the tape. Capital-markets plumbing is mutating fast: Wall Street banks arranging a record $60bn chip financing for Broadcom/Anthropic, the Texas Stock Exchange opening with ~$100bn of listings, and Anthropic prepping what could be the largest IPO ever. The consumer is bifurcating hard — TJX raised FY27 guidance while Costco's stock falls with packed lots, car buyers stretch loans, mortgage rates hit three-year highs and the unemployment rate climbed. Health Care flows deteriorated further to -53 from -46, which is a direct problem for DXCM and BAX.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: a yield-relief rally with terrible internals. The 10-year backing off 2002 highs and Brent dropping below $100 removed the two things capping multiples, so the index makes highs — but it is one sector doing the work (Tech +84 vs ten sectors negative) and Barron's framing is right that equities are discounting the bond warning rather than refuting it. October hike odds at 21.6% are a fragile anchor: the regime model moved toward Reflation and Stagflation this morning, and a sticky services print or FOMC minutes that read hawkish reverses the entire oil-and-yield relief trade in a session. Trade the confirmed cash flows, not the beta: Zscaler reaffirming $3.91bn FY27 with ~19% Q1 growth at its investor day, Constellation signing a 20-year Google PPA, Anduril booking $2.9bn from the Navy, TJX raising guidance. Fade nothing that is being paid in contracted dollars; be careful with anything whose story requires the long end to fall further.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the AI capex cycle is migrating from corporate balance sheets to structured external financing — a record $60bn bank-arranged deal for Broadcom/Anthropic, DeepSeek doubling a round to $15bn, Anthropic lining up an IPO, SpaceX re-rating. That extends the build but converts it into a credit story, which means the durable earnings accrue to toll-takers on utilisation (silicon, networking, memory, the security control plane) and above all to electrons under 20-year contracts. Power demand is now the least-contested earnings stream in the market (Google/Constellation, Duke's raised 2026 outlook, Meta's seven gas plants, Southeast Asia at 5.4% demand growth) while Utilities flows sit at -84 — that gap closes. Macro drifts toward reflation-with-sticky-inflation rather than contraction: widest trade deficit since pre-tariff, Trump easing diesel rules to blunt fuel costs into midterms, a 30-year flirting with 6% and borrowing costs above nominal GDP. That combination keeps term premium elevated, keeps Real Estate (-89) and housing impaired, and keeps the consumer splitting between off-price winners and everyone else. Trade policy is the live tail: a Franco-German push for tougher EU powers against China ahead of Beijing talks, EU-China friction now reaching defense and logistics.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: three structural lines. First, compute and generation are a single capital decision — 20-year nuclear PPAs signed by advertising companies is the clearest possible statement that the scarce input is firm power, not models; owning the fuel cycle, the grid and merchant generation is the most durable claim on AI, while Real Estate and rate-sensitive hard assets lose capital allocation. Second, agents become the interface: ChatGPT at ~1bn monthly mobile users, Claude third, Meta Muse pushing personal agents into consumer hardware, Nvidia turning AI safety into containment infrastructure. Identity, delegation and runtime containment become a metered utility on every agent action — which is why cybersecurity tops the flow ranking and Zscaler can reaffirm 19% growth into a hostile tape. Third, markets themselves are being unbundled and relocated: a new Texas exchange with $100bn of listings, tokenized/24-7 venues, prediction markets, crypto PAC money shaping 32 House races, FinCEN scrapping the mixer rule. Venues, rails and brokers win; asset gatherers and the illiquidity now being pushed to households lose. Underneath it all, demography and a debt pile whose service cost exceeds nominal GDP growth make productivity-per-worker and permanent term premium the two facts everything else must price around.

short_term: Consumers are trading down and stretching: TJX raises FY27 guidance and outpaces the market while Costco's stock falls despite packed lots, and car buyers are extending loan terms to make monthly payments — the purchase is unchanged, the financing is deteriorating.

Housing demand is being converted into rental politics: mortgage rates at a near-three-year high plus a rising unemployment rate are locking buyers out, and America's renters are organising as a political movement rather than waiting for affordability.

Firms are paying for AI with headcount: Visa taking $563m of job-cut costs while reporting resilient consumer spending is the template — spending holds up even as the labour income that funds it is being optimised away.

Retail attention has rotated to stablecoins (+51% search), TikTok commerce (+52%) and AI data centers — people are simultaneously seeking yield/alternatives to banks and entertainment-native shopping.
Investors are chasing a single sector: Tech flows +84 against ten negative sectors and growth over value by 99 points means positioning risk, not conviction, is now the dominant variable.
Energy cost is politically salient enough that policy responds directly — dyed diesel allowed on highways ahead of midterms is a consumer-pocketbook intervention, not an energy policy.
long_term: Delegation of cognitive work to agents becomes default behaviour: a billion monthly mobile users on one assistant means people now outsource search, drafting and decision-prep, which permanently reallocates attention away from ad-funded surfaces toward agent surfaces.

Electricity becomes a visible household and sovereign security issue — Singapore eyeing nuclear after import shocks, Southeast Asia straining at 5.4% demand growth, El Niño raising prices — and 'energy security' joins food and housing as a thing voters buy politically.
Security shifts from a product to a continuous metered permission layer on every automated action, because the counterparty is increasingly a machine acting on your behalf.

Market access is becoming always-on and geographically dispersed (Texas exchange, tokenized venues, prediction markets), normalising trading as a consumer entertainment and status activity rather than a periodic savings act.

Health consumption bifurcates between cheap pharmacological fixes (GLP-1 normalisation, Ozempic queries steady) and expensive continuous monitoring/devices, with payer pressure and deteriorating sector flows squeezing anything in between.

Physical AI enters consumer imagination — humanoid robot search rising with 'for sale' and 'price' as top queries — which pulls forward demand for automation in labour-scarce, demographically shrinking economies.
